key_insight: Safeguarded online learning can improve nonlinear conjugate gradient robustness while retaining classical search directions, low storage, and deterministic recovery mechanisms.
engineering_relevance: The approach is promising for PDE-constrained optimization where expensive function and gradient evaluations make reliable progress especially valuable.
method: Use one online extreme learning machine to predict NCG coefficients during restart recovery or persistent stagnation.
Use a second model only after line-search failure to propose a bounded correction to the fallback step size.
Accept predictions only under deterministic numerical safeguards; train online from existing trajectory data without extra function or gradient evaluations.
evidence_signal: Tests on 480 CUTEst problems showed improved robustness across six NCG variants at broadly comparable evaluation costs; a PDE conductivity-identification example illustrated potential cost and runtime savings.
watch_item: Benefits depend on safeguard and out-of-distribution checks; the abstract does not quantify gains or establish broad PDE generalization.
paper_title: Safeguarded Learning-Assisted Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient Methods
